confirmed.claim: For template 'convert' the goal's `must` is only [kind(<target>/<name>.md)=file, ext(...)=md] and `ext` is name-derived (already true while absent), so the only effective requirement is 'some file exists at that path'. This is not a leak, but it is a task-validity defect inside the generator (in scope for the generator/target-name check) and it affects by_template numbers and any claim about what C learned.

Severity: negligible; at most a note that the "예측오류/예측" column aggregates ok-mispredictions and attribute-mispredictions without breakdown (per-step records.jsonl keep 'ok' and 'pred_error' separately, so it is recoverable).

summaries.summary:
Scope: read README, RESEARCH_CONTRACT, BOOTSTRAP_MANIFEST, EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL, DECISIONS, protocol.json and every .py under atanor_os/ (world, core, agent, eval, tests). Files changed on disk mid-review (models.py/generator.py 01:57, protocol.json 01:58, run.py 02:00); all were re-read against the current state and the findings refer to current content. `python -m pytest atanor_os/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider`: 9 passed. No repository file was modified; probe snippets wrote only to temp dirs. The in-progress pilot (results/p1-test-01, seed 1, 300 explore steps, tests ran) was not touched.

Leakage lens - checked and CLEAN: (1) Import direction: agent/, core/, world/ import nothing from eval/ (verified per file; lift->world, models->world/bootstrap/lift/rule_learner, planner->world, loop->core/world/planner). eval/ importing agent (oracle uses agent.planner.plan and agent.lift.apply_effects; explore uses agent.lift.lifted_pre) is the allowed direction. (2) Shared constants: BUDGET, TARGET, WORDS_*, TEMPLATES, POOL live only in eval/; the learner receives only Workspace + Goal(must/keep/capabilities/budget/universe). (3) Names: WORDS_TRAIN and WORDS_TEST are disjoint, test target names (archive/bins/rendered/out) never appear in exploration, and lifting abstracts names away entirely, so name patterns cannot help any condition. (4) agent/bootstrap.py DOCS encodes effects only (equal to oracle TRUE_EFFECTS except convert's hash) and no preconditions; this is declared in BOOTSTRAP §2. Side note: because DOCS==TRUE_EFFECTS, the manifest's §6 learning target 'undocumented effects' is empty; C's 'learned' status is still honest because its effects are re-derived from post-states, not read from DOCS. (5) agent/planner.py has no domain-specific heuristics (no mkdir/copy knowledge); tool enumeration order (mkdir, copy, move, delete, convert; sorted paths) only breaks exact f-ties and is identical for all conditions. (6) The `avoid` set in agent/loop.py is generic episode-internal memory (root actions that failed in this exact canon state, reset on state change), documented in BOOTSTRAP §4, identical across conditions; it gives every condition trial-and-error recovery (e.g. A can finish a 'convert' task by exhausting root copies then mkdir), which compresses C-B but is not a leak. (7) No per-case exceptions for known failures anywhere in agent/ (rule_learner flags unseparable failures instead of hiding them). (8) The 01:57 models.py refactor (shared `sig` computed once in CouncilModel.predict) is semantically neutral; TrueModel.predict has no `sig` parameter but is never called with one. (9) reachable()/ORACLE only observe and predict on the task workspace; they never execute, so the agent's workspace is not pre-touched. (10) frozen mode never calls model.update; --adapt deep-copies the base model per task, so no cross-task carry-over.

Real issues found (none is a direct answer injection): one medium task-validity defect in the generator ('convert' template completes by copying any file, so convert and its preconditions are never tested; the evaluator's own ORACLE plan copies the keep-file), one medium verdict/guard gap (new --skip-tests leaves tests_passed=None, which verdict() does not treat as INVALID, so the leak tests become optional for a VALID verdict), and four low items: the leakage test's regex misses `from .. import eval`/importlib forms (no current violation), protocol text overstates test novelty (json never generated, md and depth-2 already in the train log, depth unrepresented), exploration novelty is keyed on B's retrieval key with REPEAT=2 (fair and pre-registered but a declared sensitivity, not task-specific help), and the untracked/edited-after-launch code has no recorded identity in results.

Scope: read atanor_os README/RESEARCH_CONTRACT/BOOTSTRAP_MANIFEST/EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL/DECISIONS and all Python under world/, core/, agent/, eval/, tests/; ran the test suite (9 passed) and read-only snippets over the existing experience logs (runs/dev1, runs/x1, runs/x300_*) and dev1 records; nothing in the repository was modified and the in-progress pilot was not run. Note: agent/models.py, eval/generator.py, eval/run.py, EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL.md and DECISIONS.md changed on disk during the review (time cap 5->10 s, shared council signature, --skip-tests/--label); findings are against the current files.

Fairness verdict by question. (1) B is not weakened by a bug, but its exact key (kind/ext/parent_kind per role + same_content) is coverage-starved after 300 random steps: 38-79% exact hits along ORACLE plans on dev, 57-66% on test, with the rest falling to docs 'always succeeds'; dev shows B=0.375 on name-only changes where the protocol claims B should match C, so C-B partly measures coverage, not induction (medium). (2) D as defined can only lose to C: members hold strict subsets and the induction only keeps literals that a failure in that subset demands, and a member with no success votes 'success' via docs; on dev/test initial states D makes 499/2206 false-success predictions vs C 23/158 and zero false-fails for either, D mispredicts its own training convert experiences, and dev D convert completion equals A's (medium). (3) The only effectively unequal budget is the wall-clock planning cap: D (3x prediction cost, A-like branching) hit it and abstained 8/24 dev episodes vs 0 for C; the cap also makes D-C machine/load dependent (medium). (4) Verified non-findings: RuleModel.predict never reaching retrieval when a rule exists is harmless (0 contradictions between C's rule and B's index across 5 logs, since the induction admits every success signature and excludes every explained failure); B's majority tie cannot occur (0 mixed-outcome signatures in 6 logs, the signature determines the outcome); frozen mode shares an immutable base model and reset_stats makes council counters per-episode; CouncilModel.update round-robin keeps thirds disjoint and is adapt-only; the +0.5 'documented' penalty and the action enumeration are applied uniformly by status/universe. (5) ORACLE only diagnoses: reachable() plans with TrueModel without executing, learner models never receive TrueModel or its output, exploration does not use it, and the leakage tests pass. Two low findings: harness code edited after freeze during the frozen run and a --skip-tests replication still prints a VALID_* verdict; and a latent representation asymmetry in pred_error accounting (B emits content-specific hash constants, C can emit 'unknown').

Lens: evaluation and verdict logic of atanor_os/ (read all .py under world/, core/, agent/, eval/, tests/ plus the four docs; ran pytest (9 passed), replicated semantic_check coverage, enumerated the test split, probed the planner on test tasks, and mined the finished runs atanor_os/runs/dev1 and atanor_os/runs/oracle_test). Nothing wrong found for: judge() independence (re-observes the real workspace, never reads the model; agent_believes_done is a separate field); paired() per-task/per-seed math (rate() averages over the other axis, ties counted as >=0 per protocol wording); ORACLE completion < 1.0 is detected (metrics.py:67, ORACLE appended on the first seed, and test tasks are seed-independent so one ORACLE pass covers all 20); dev/test seeding (random.Random(f'{split}-{index}') and 'explore-{seed}' are disjoint; WORDS_TRAIN/WORDS_TEST/POOL names disjoint); learning cost is timed separately in build_model(); tracemalloc peaks did not show order drift in dev1. Real problems found, most severe first: (1) the 'convert' template's must literals (kind=file, ext=md) are satisfied by copy, and ext of an absent path already holds, so the template never tests convert and partial starts at 0.5 — confirmed in real records (ORACLE/C solve every convert task with copy only); (2) planner node/time budget exhaustion is recorded as 'abstained', never 'budget_exceeded' (all 8 D abstains in dev1 are 5 s clock hits, so D effectively runs with ~118 nodes vs C's 600); (3) semantic_check has fixed seed 7 and no coverage accounting: mkdir success verified once, convert success twice in 300 checks; (4) test split novelty is thinner than EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL claims (json never generated, md already in exploration, 11/20 tasks carry no unseen attribute); (5) pred_errors scores a doc/retrieved prediction silent about hash as an error on every successful convert; plus low-severity bookkeeping gaps (unreachable counted per condition, storage not per condition, completed ignores mid-episode keep violation, blocked structurally zero, no code identity in env_info while BUDGET demonstrably changed between runs, learner-performance test inside the INVALID gate, records written only at the end of pilot).
